newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUNDS FIRMER AS FEARS WANE OF BUBA REPO MOVE.
newsitem.headline: BUNDS FIRMER AS FEARS WANE OF BUBA REPO MOVE.

text.p: Bunds firmed slightly early on Monday amid short-covering after Friday's losses, but dealers said major gains were unlikely and that Bunds would fall back to losses if they fail to breach technical resistance.

September Bunds were quoted at 101.81 at 0720 GMT, up 20 basis points from Friday's close, breaching key resistance at 101.75. Bunds were drawing support from the weakening of the dollar in recent sessions which dampened fears of an imminent Bundesbank credit tightening to defend the mark, dealers said.
The dollar was trading around just below 1.85 marks at 0720 GMT, four pfennigs below the high it reached last week.

"The probability that the Bundesbank will do something tomorrow has gone down a lot," one dealer said. Speculation grew last week that the Bundesbank may signal higher money market rates by switching to a variable-rate repo.

The Bundesbank is due to announce on Tuesday what form its repo allocation for this week will take -- an unchanged fixed repo at 3.00 percent, a variable repo, a repo at a higher rate or a combination of a fixed and a variable-rate repo.
Dealers said scope for upmove was limited on Monday.
"If we breach 101.75 we'll have room to move up to 101.94. If not we can quickly fall to 101.50," one Frankfurt-based trader said. If 101.50 failed to hold, the next support level was 101.42.
The 101.42 level was a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the June and July rally.

Dealers are waiting for a flood of data this week. German final cost of living data for July and retail sales for June are due on Tuesday or Wednesday, followed by wholesale prices on Wednesday or Thursday.

U.S. data this week include unit labour costs and productivity for the second quarter on Tuesday as well as July retail sales and producer prices on Wednesday. Thursday sees the release of weekly jobless claims and July consumer prices.
